Rashi on Sanhedrin 24a:10:1.hebrew: להטמין את הצונן - מים צונן ומתיירא שלא יוחמו, אסור להטמינן בחול צונן (לצורך שבת) [בשבת]:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 24a:10:1.english: To insulate that which is cold - [Such as] cold water, and [one] is afraid that it will become warm — it is prohibited to insulate it in cold sand (for the purpose of Shabbat) [on Shabbat].

Rashi on Sanhedrin 24a:10:2.hebrew: הורה זקן - ר' יוסי, דאזלינן בתריה:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 24a:10:2.english: An elder has ruled - [This refers to] Rabbi Yose, whose [ruling] we follow.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 24a:11:1.english: Filled the place of his fathers - [He was] as distinguished as his father.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 24a:12:1.hebrew: מחבלים - בלשון עז וחמה מקשין זה לזה. ובני א"י נוחין יחד ומעיינין יחד, ומתקן זה את דברי זה, והשמועה יוצאה לאור:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 24a:12:1.english: [Who] injure - With harsh and angry language they raise difficulties against one another. But the people of Eretz Yisrael are gentle with one another and deliberate together, and one corrects the words of the other, and the teaching comes to light.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 24a:13:1.english: [They] oil [one another] - [They are] pleasant like oil.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 24a:14:1.english: [The] ephah - This is the evil inclination.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 24a:14:2.english: Two women - [These are] flattery and arrogance.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 24a:14:3.english: And the wind was in their wings - An expression of arrogance.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 24a:14:4.hebrew: ככנפי החסידה - זו חנופה, שמראין עצמם חסידים:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 24a:14:4.english: Like the wings of a stork - This is flattery, for they show themselves [to be] pious.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 24a:16:1.hebrew: לבנות לה בית - ולא כתיב (להם), אלמא האחת לבדה נתישבה שם:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 24a:16:1.english: To build her a house - And it is not written: “[for] them,” which shows that only one [of them] settled there.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 24a:17:1.hebrew: עניות תורה - בעילם היא. דניאל בעילם הוה, דכתיב (דניאל ח׳:ב׳): "ואני (הייתי) בשושן הבירה אשר בעילם המדינה", ולא רבץ תורה. עזרא הוה בבבל, ולמד חק ומשפט בישראל:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 24a:17:1.english: Poverty of Torah - [This] was in Eilam. Daniel was in Eilam, as it is written: “And I [was] in Shushan the capital, which is in the province of Eilam” (Daniel 8:2), and he did not disseminate Torah. Ezra was in Babylonia, and taught statute and ordinance in Israel.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 24a:18:1.hebrew: במחשכים הושיבני - שאין נוחין זה עם זה, ותלמודם ספק בידם:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 24a:18:1.english: He has made me dwell in dark places - For they are not agreeable with one another, and their study is in doubt in their hands.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 24a:19:1.english: [He is] trusted by me - To be a judge.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 24a:19:2.hebrew: אבא - פסול מן התורה לדונני, לא לזכות ולא לחיוב, דנפקא לן בפירקין (דף כז:) מלא יומתו אבות על בנים וגו':
Rashi on Sanhedrin 24a:19:2.english: My father - [He is] disqualified by Torah law from judging me, neither to acquit nor to convict, as we derive in our chapter (27b) from: “The fathers shall not be put to death for the children,” etc.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 24a:1:1.hebrew: בעדים פסולים ודיינין כשרין - בעל דין פוסל הדיינין והעדים, ונמצאו דבריו אמת על העדים, ומשום הכי מהימנינן ליה אפי' לגבי דיינין:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 24a:1:1.english: With disqualified witnesses and fit judges - A litigant disqualifies the judges and the witnesses, and his words were found to be true regarding the witnesses, and because of this we believe him even regarding the judges.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 24a:1:2.hebrew: סיפא - שנמצאו דבריו אמת על הדיינין שפסולין הם, ומשום הכי מהימנינן להו אעדים אליבא דר"מ. ורבנן לית להו מיגו:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 24a:1:2.english: The latter clause - [A case] where his words were found to be true regarding the judges, that they are disqualified, and for this reason we believe him regarding the witnesses according to Rabbi Meir. And the Rabbis do not accept [the principle of] migo.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 24a:20:1.english: Vow to me - An expression of an oath.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 24a:20:2.english: He can retract - And demand a full oath.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 24a:21:1.hebrew: דקבליה עליה בחד - דיינא, ואע"ג דאיכא תרי אחריני בהדיה, א"ר מאיר יכול לחזור בו:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 24a:21:1.english: Where he accepted him upon himself as one - [As one] judge; and even though there are two others with him, Rabbi Meir says [that] he can retract.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 24a:22:1.hebrew: במחול לך - אי תובע אמר לנתבע: "נאמן עלי אבא או אביך, אם יזכוך — יהא מחול לך" — התם קאמרי רבנן אינו יכול לחזור בו, דהא זכה זה במה שבידו, מכיון שיצא זכאי:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 24a:22:1.english: [In the case of] “Forgiven to you” - If the claimant said to the defendant: “My father is acceptable to me, or your father [is acceptable to me]; if they rule in your favor, it shall be forgiven to you” — there the Rabbis say [that] he cannot retract, for this [defendant] has acquired that which is in his possession, once he emerged vindicated.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 24a:22:2.hebrew: אבל באתן לך - דנתבע אמר לתובע: אם יחייבוני אבא או אביך, אתן לך:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 24a:22:2.english: But in [a case of] “I will give you” - Where the defendant said to the claimant: “If my father or your father finds me liable, I will give [it] to you.”

Rashi on Sanhedrin 24a:22:3.hebrew: דברי הכל יכול לחזור - דהואיל והממון בידו, אין בו כח לתובע להוציא אלא בדיינין כשרין:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 24a:22:3.english: Everyone agrees that he can retract - For since the money is in his possession, the claimant has no power to extract [it] except through qualified judges.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 24a:26:1.english: He is stating his own reasoning - And he disagrees with both of them.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 24a:2:1.english: There is another court - And [the judge] has no personal stake in the testimony.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 24a:5:1.hebrew: רבין סבר - אמרינן מיגו בעלמא. כדקיימא הכא, טעמא משום מיגו הוא, ואי לאו הכי הוא — לא הוה פסיל רבי מאיר. ולרב דימי, לא אמרי' מיגו בעלמא:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 24a:5:1.english: Ravin holds - We say [the principle of] miggo in general. As [the case] stands here, the reason is because of miggo, and were it not so, Rabbi Meir would not have disqualified [them]. And according to Rav Dimi, we do not say miggo in general.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 24a:7:1.hebrew: וטוחנן זה בזה - מטיח ומקיש זה בזה. אלמא חריפא טובא הוה, מקרי ליה לר' מאיר דרך ענוה: ״פה קדוש״:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 24a:7:1.english: And grinding them into each other - [He] strikes and knocks [them] against each other. This shows that he was extremely sharp; [yet] he called Rabbi Meir “a holy mouth” out of humility.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 24a:8:1.hebrew: אמר רבינא - ומאי תמהא? והלא ר' מאיר עוקר הרי הרים הוא, כלומר: אלים וגבר טפי טובא:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 24a:8:1.english: Ravina said - And what is the wonder? Is not Rabbi Meir an uprooter of towering mountains? That is to say, [he was] far more powerful and superior.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 24a:9:1.hebrew: בא וראה כמה - כלומר, לא אתמוהי קא מתמהי, אלא הכי קאמר: ״בא וראה כמה בני ארץ ישראל מחבבין זה את זה״. דהא ריש לקיש חריף וחכים טובא הוה, וקרי ליה לר' מאיר ״פה קדוש״ — דקא מחבב ליה, ומיישב את הדבר להתקיים:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 24a:9:1.english: Come and see how much - That is to say, [the Gemara] was not expressing astonishment; rather, this is what it is saying: “Come and see how much the people of Eretz Yisrael love each other!” For Reish Lakish was exceedingly sharp and wise, and [yet] he called Rabbi Meir “a holy mouth,” because he loved him and resolved the matter so that it could be upheld.

Tosafot on Sanhedrin 24a:18:1.hebrew: בלולה במקרא ובמשנה וכו' - פירש רבינו תם, דבתלמוד שלנו אנו פוטרין עצמנו ממה שאמרו חכמים (מסכת ע"ג דף יט.): "לעולם ישלש אדם שנותיו: שליש במקרא, שליש במשנה, שליש בש"ס". אע"פ כן, אנו קוראים בכל יום פרשת התמיד, ושונים במשנת "איזהו מקומן", וגורסין "רבי ישמעאל אומר: בשלש עשרה מדות" וכו':
Tosafot on Sanhedrin 24a:18:1.english: “Mixed with Bible, and with Mishna, etc.” - Rabbeinu Tam explained that through our Talmud we exempt ourselves from what the Sages said (tractate Avodah Zarah 19b): “A person should always divide his years into three: one-third in Bible, one-third in Mishna, and one-third in Shas Talmud.” Even so, we read each day the section of the Daily Offering, and we study the Mishnah of “Which are the places” Eizehu Mekoman, and we recite: “Rabbi Yishmael says: Through thirteen hermeneutical principles the Torah is expounded,” etc.

Tosafot on Sanhedrin 24a:21:1.hebrew: אמר רב דימי כגון דקבליה עליה בחד - פירש הקונט' דאפילו הכי קאמר ר' מאיר דיכול לחזור בו. ולא נהירא, דכיון דלרבותא נקטיה, הוה ליה למימר "לא צריכא כו'", דמדקאמר "כגון" משמע דדוקא קא אמר: כגון דקבליה עליה בחד. על כן נראה דאמילתייהו דרבנן קאי: דדוקא כגון דקבלוה עלויה בחד, דחדא לריעותא הוא דאיכא, קאמרי רבנן דאינו יכול לחזור בו; אבל אי קבליה עליה כבי תרי, יכול לחזור בו אף לרבנן, כיון דאיכא תרתי לריעותא:
Tosafot on Sanhedrin 24a:21:1.english: Rav Dimi said: For example, where he accepted him upon himself as one - Rashi explained that even so, Rabbi Meir says that he can retract. But this does not appear correct, for since he cited it to teach a novelty, [the Gemara] should have said: "No, it is necessary, etc.," as from the fact that it says "For example" [kegon], it implies that it means specifically: such as where he accepted him upon himself as one [judge]. Therefore, it appears that [Rav Dimi's statement] refers to the words of the Rabbis: that specifically [in a case] such as where they accepted him upon themselves as one [judge], where there is only a single deficiency, do the Rabbis say that he cannot retract; but if he accepted him upon himself as two [judges], he can retract even according to the Rabbis, since there are two deficiencies.
